correctness.rationale: For a fixed cointegral basis, the proof gives a bijective parameterization of degree-one chain extensions by a center vector and solves the resulting weighted \(\ell^1_2\) one-center problem exactly through the linear isometry \((r,s)\mapsto(r+s,r-s)\). Cointegral bases correspond to independent integral coordinate columns for the two integral cycle generators. Every such pair has the three nonzero vectors \(u\), \(v\), and \(u-v\), not all of \(\ell^1\)-norm one; the three possible norm-two placements are realized by explicit unimodular pairs. This yields the claimed closed form for all permitted lengths and every subfield \(F\subset\mathbb R\). The finite verifier checks exact arithmetic consistency only and is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Three-path theta graphs are the natural first rank-two family with overlapping simple cycles. The formula gives a genuine structural boundary for the reciprocal-girth phenomenon: it is exact only in the long-third-path regime \(c\ge2a+b\), while overlap forces the second scale \(2/(b+c)\) otherwise and produces a factor-two gap in the equilateral case. This is a motivated exact family calculation for a newly introduced invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a parameter renaming.
